purpose: Crosswalk only explicitly named places in the 2025 CC BY checklist to administrative context using official local-government/PSGC pages and an independent published locality anchor. This is not a Ragay Gulf boundary or a complete fish inventory.

rules: Keep the article locality and historical date/catalog spelling unchanged.

Use exact municipality or named-feature matches for administrative context; an identical named point in independent literature can anchor the locality name but does not transfer that other specimen’s coordinates.
Do not turn a broad gulf-only phrase into province/region presence, a georeferenced specimen record, or a legal water boundary.
Official administrative webpages are cited for names and relationships only; no image, geometry, or bulk page content is reused.

localityCrosswalks.decision: The exact locality string is independently reported with Camarines Sur for a different CAS specimen. Use that only as a named-point administrative anchor for the locality phrase; do not copy CAS 34193 coordinates, depth, or identity to CAS 34197/CAS 47781.

The Quezon Provincial Government lists Alibijaban Island under its San Andres municipality page. This supports a named-island administrative context only; the checklist provides no specimen coordinates and does not show whether the marine collection point lies within any municipal-water boundary.

Held: the article spelling differs from the official page’s Alibijaban. No alias authority was found to equate them; do not normalize to the Quezon island by spelling resemblance.

localityCrosswalks.articleEntries: remaining source-reported Ragay Gulf/Ragay Bay lots in the 16-treatment batch
localityCrosswalks.decision: Held: generic gulf/bay phrases and other named points/islands (including Canmahala/Canmahana, Saboon, Anima Sola, Buri, Pusgo, Caurusan, Nagas, Rogo, and Bantuin) were not assigned to a province or region in this step. No gulf polygon was sourced.

limitations: This is a historical literature locality crosswalk, not an ecological survey, current-presence claim, full local fish checklist, or proof of catchability.
Named-island/municipality context is not a substitute for marine coordinates, municipal-water boundaries, fishing access, or jurisdiction.
Siburio Point is anchored by a different CAS specimen in the 2013 paper; no coordinates or measurement from CAS 34193 is transferred to the 2025 checklist lots.
The 2025 article’s taxonomy conflict, catalog-number discrepancy, and uncatalogued Ostorhinchus parvulus lot identity remain unresolved.
GBIF/CAS occurrence candidates remain held under their separate record-level reuse and locality review; this CC BY article does not override CAS database terms.
nextAction: Continue with the other locality names only when primary locality or official geographic evidence is available; seek a suitable licensed locality gazetteer/authoritative maritime source before creating points or boundaries. Keep generic gulf-only lots unassigned and continue the freshwater/marine regional inventory in parallel.
